item.title: Sunny Skies, Lower Humidity Expected Through Friday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola area residents can expect pleasant weather conditions through the end of the week, with sunny skies and lower humidity levels making for comfortable outdoor conditions. Thursday will bring mostly sunny skies with highs near 89 degrees, according to the National Weather Service. Light east winds of 5 to 10 mph are expected, with gusts…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola area residents can expect pleasant weather conditions through the end of the week, with sunny skies and lower humidity levels making for comfortable outdoor conditions.

Thursday will bring mostly sunny skies with highs near 89 degrees, according to the National Weather Service. Light east winds of 5 to 10 mph are expected, with gusts reaching up to 20 mph. Overnight Thursday into Friday morning will remain clear with lows dropping to around 68 degrees and calm winds.

Friday looks even nicer, with sunny conditions continuing and highs climbing to near 91 degrees. East winds around 5 mph will become calm by afternoon, making for an ideal day for outdoor activities. The lower humidity levels accompanying this weather system should provide some relief from the typical summer mugginess.

Those planning outdoor plans through Friday should take advantage of the clear, stable weather pattern before conditions potentially shift over the weekend.

item.content:encoded: The Tate Aggies picked up a varsity volleyball win Tuesday night, defeating the visiting Pace Patriots 3-1 on their home court. item.title: Vehicle Fire Extinguished at Davisville Community Center
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Firefighters quickly brought a vehicle fire under control Wednesday afternoon in front of the Davisville Community Center on Highway 97, according to reports from the scene. The blaze broke out while the vehicle was in motion on the highway before coming to rest near the community center. No injuries were reported as a result of the incident.…
item.content:encoded: Firefighters quickly brought a vehicle fire under control Wednesday afternoon in front of the Davisville Community Center on Highway 97, according to reports from the scene. The blaze broke out while the vehicle was in motion on the highway before coming to rest near the community center. No injuries were reported as a result of the incident. Because the fire occurred while the vehicle was actively traveling on Highway 97, the Florida Highway Patrol has assumed the investigation into what caused the flames to ignite.

item.description: An Escambia County man will spend the next 25 years in state prison following his conviction for a fatal shooting at a local gas station last year. Arrington Marcellas Moultrie, 37, was found guilty of second-degree murder, shooting into a vehicle, and tampering with physical evidence related to the 2024 incident. According to court records,…
item.content:encoded:
An Escambia County man will spend the next 25 years in state prison following his conviction for a fatal shooting at a local gas station last year.

Arrington Marcellas Moultrie, 37, was found guilty of second-degree murder, shooting into a vehicle, and tampering with physical evidence related to the 2024 incident. According to court records, Moultrie was sentenced to the two-and-a-half-decade prison term as a result of the convictions.

The case highlights ongoing concerns about gun violence in Escambia County. Authorities did not immediately release additional details about the circumstances of the shooting or the victim's identity.

item.title: Escambia Animal Welfare Rescues Fox Tangled in Netting Near Molino
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A red fox is on the mend after getting trapped in netting on a property near Molino, thanks to quick work by Escambia County Animal Welfare officers. A resident on Stout Road spotted the distressed animal and called animal welfare dispatch for help. Sergeants Roberson and Agrecy responded to the scene and carefully freed the fox from the netting…
item.content:encoded:
A red fox is on the mend after getting trapped in netting on a property near Molino, thanks to quick work by Escambia County Animal Welfare officers.

A resident on Stout Road spotted the distressed animal and called animal welfare dispatch for help. Sergeants Roberson and Agrecy responded to the scene and carefully freed the fox from the netting that had become wrapped around it.

"Our officers were able to safely remove the netting and the fox is now recovering," according to the incident report from Escambia County Animal Welfare. The agency reminds property owners to secure netting and other materials that could trap wildlife, and to contact animal welfare immediately if they encounter an injured or entangled animal. Residents can reach Escambia County Animal Welfare dispatch for wildlife emergencies.

item.title: Impact 100 Names 20 Nonprofit Finalists for $1.3M in Grants
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Impact 100 Pensacola Bay Area has selected 20 nonprofit organizations as finalists to compete for more than $1.3 million in grants, marking a milestone year for the women-led philanthropic organization. Thirteen of the 20 finalists will each receive grants of $101,000 during Impact 100's Annual Meeting scheduled for October 11. The grants…
item.content:encoded:
Impact 100 Pensacola Bay Area has selected 20 nonprofit organizations as finalists to compete for more than $1.3 million in grants, marking a milestone year for the women-led philanthropic organization.

Thirteen of the 20 finalists will each receive grants of $101,000 during Impact 100's Annual Meeting scheduled for October 11. The grants represent the organization's commitment to supporting community nonprofits across the Pensacola Bay Area.

The announcement comes as Impact 100 celebrates record membership. The organization now has 1,313 women members in 2026, an all-time high. Members pool their donations to support high-impact nonprofits through a competitive selection process, with each member having a vote in determining grant recipients.

item.title: Century Town Council Delays Decision on Street Department Employee Firing
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Century Town Council has postponed action this week on a proposed termination of a street department employee facing allegations of gross negligence and causing financial hardship to residents, according to reporting from North Escambia. Under the town's charter, the mayor must obtain council approval before hiring or terminating municipal…
item.content:encoded:
The Century Town Council has postponed action this week on a proposed termination of a street department employee facing allegations of gross negligence and causing financial hardship to residents, according to reporting from North Escambia.

Under the town's charter, the mayor must obtain council approval before hiring or terminating municipal employees. The delayed vote suggests the council wanted additional time to review the case against the worker before moving forward with dismissal proceedings.

Details on the specific incidents cited in the negligence allegations were not immediately disclosed. The tabling of the motion means the matter will likely return to council at a future meeting for further deliberation and a final vote.

item.title: Tate High Teacher Wins $1,000 Sun Belt Conference Award
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Tate High School educator was surprised with national recognition and a $1,000 award Wednesday as part of an annual initiative to honor outstanding teachers. Lauralee Best received the gift from representatives of the Sun Belt Conference during a "Big Day for Teachers" event sponsored by the College Football Foundation. The Extra Yard for…
item.content:encoded:
A Tate High School educator was surprised with national recognition and a $1,000 award Wednesday as part of an annual initiative to honor outstanding teachers. Lauralee Best received the gift from representatives of the Sun Belt Conference during a "Big Day for Teachers" event sponsored by the College Football Foundation.

The Extra Yard for Teachers program celebrates educators across the country who make significant contributions to their students and communities. The award provides funds teachers can direct toward classroom needs or professional development.

Best's recognition reflects the Sun Belt's broader commitment to supporting education in communities across its member institutions' footprint. The conference has recognized teachers through this initiative for several years, highlighting the intersection between college athletics and K-12 education.

item.title: Alzheimer's Walk Coming to Foley in November
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Mobile Bay Walk to End Alzheimer's will take place November 14 at OWA Parks and Recreation in Foley, according to event organizers. The annual walk raises awareness and funds for Alzheimer's research and support services across the Mobile Bay region, which includes nearby communities in Northwest Florida. item.content:encoded:
The Mobile Bay Walk to End Alzheimer's will take place November 14 at OWA Parks and Recreation in Foley, according to event organizers. The annual walk raises awareness and funds for Alzheimer's research and support services across the Mobile Bay region, which includes nearby communities in Northwest Florida.

The event brings together families, caregivers, and community members affected by Alzheimer's disease. Participants typically walk to honor those living with the disease and remember those lost to it.

For more information about registration, sponsorship opportunities, or to learn how to participate, organizers encourage interested residents to contact the event coordinators directly.

Semmes, located north of Mobile, hosts the festival as an annual tradition to bring the community together. More details about specific vendors and activities are expected to be announced as the event date approaches.

item.title: Hospitality Workers Train for Medical Emergencies in Pensacola Area
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hospitality workers across the Pensacola area are getting equipped with lifesaving emergency response skills through a partnership between Ascension Sacred Heart and Visit Pensacola. The training initiative, held in Perdido Key, aims to prepare hotel, restaurant, and tourism industry employees to recognize and respond quickly to medical…
item.content:encoded:
Hospitality workers across the Pensacola area are getting equipped with lifesaving emergency response skills through a partnership between Ascension Sacred Heart and Visit Pensacola.

The training initiative, held in Perdido Key, aims to prepare hotel, restaurant, and tourism industry employees to recognize and respond quickly to medical emergencies. According to WKRG News 5, the emphasis is on being ready to act decisively when situations arise, whether during peak tourist season or slower months.

Ascension Sacred Heart and Visit Pensacola designed the program to ensure that frontline hospitality staff—who often encounter guests and visitors in vulnerable situations—know basic emergency protocols and can provide immediate assistance before first responders arrive.

The partnership underscores growing recognition in the tourism industry that trained staff can make a critical difference in emergency outcomes. As one of Northwest Florida's major economic engines, the hospitality sector regularly brings thousands of visitors to Pensacola beaches and attractions year-round, making emergency preparedness among workers an ongoing priority.

item.title: Milton Fire Department lands $25K grant for life-saving equipment

The funding will go toward purchasing new equipment designed to improve the department's ability to respond to…
item.content:encoded:
The Milton Fire Department has secured more than $25,000 in funding to upgrade its emergency response capabilities. According to a department announcement, MFD received a $25,195 grant through the Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation.

The funding will go toward purchasing new equipment designed to improve the department's ability to respond to emergencies and save lives in the Santa Rosa County community. The Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation regularly awards grants to fire departments across the country to help them obtain critical gear and technology.

Milton Fire officials said the grant will help ensure the department remains equipped with modern, reliable tools for firefighting and rescue operations.

item.content:encoded:
Motorists traveling between Pensacola and Mobile should plan for delays as a portion of the I-10 Causeway in Spanish Fort will temporarily close for bridge repair work, according to WKRG News 5.

The closure will span parts of two days, though specific dates and times for the work have not yet been announced. The causeway is a critical corridor for traffic between the Pensacola area and points east, carrying significant daily commuter and commercial traffic.

Drivers are urged to monitor traffic updates and consider using alternate routes during the scheduled closure. Additional details about the exact timing and nature of the bridge repairs are expected to be released as the work date approaches.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Gears Up for 59th Annual Farm Tour
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County is preparing to welcome visitors back to its annual farm tour, a nearly six-decade-old tradition that showcases the region's agricultural heritage and working farms. The farm tour, now in its 59th year, offers residents and visitors a chance to see local farming operations up close and learn about the crops and livestock that…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is preparing to welcome visitors back to its annual farm tour, a nearly six-decade-old tradition that showcases the region's agricultural heritage and working farms.

The farm tour, now in its 59th year, offers residents and visitors a chance to see local farming operations up close and learn about the crops and livestock that define the area's rural economy. According to WKRG News 5, the event continues to be a popular draw for those interested in agriculture and rural life in Northwest Florida.

The farm tour has become a staple event for Santa Rosa County, reflecting the importance of agriculture to the local community and providing an educational opportunity for families to connect with the land and farming practices in the region.

item.title: IMPACT 100 names 13 local groups for $101K in grants

According to a news release, the grants represent the organization's commitment to supporting charitable work across the Pensacola area. The selected groups will use the funding to advance…
item.content:encoded:
IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area has announced its 2026 grant finalists, directing $101,000 in funding to 13 local organizations working on community projects. According to a news release, the grants represent the organization's commitment to supporting charitable work across the Pensacola area.

The selected groups will use the funding to advance various initiatives benefiting residents throughout the region. IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area pools donations from members to award significant grants to vetted nonprofits and community-focused organizations.

The full list of finalist organizations and their specific projects is available through IMPACT 100's announcement. Residents interested in learning more about the grant recipients or the organization's work can contact IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area directly for additional details.
